title: Amp-Turn, Oersted, A/m: Magnetic Field Strength Units
h1: Magnetic field strength units — A/m, ampere-turn and oersted
description: 1 Oe = 79.577 A/m. Amp-turn = current × turns and drives H directly. Coil designers, transformer engineers and NDT technicians all need this table.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: H is what the current produces; B is what the material responds. Get the input unit wrong and B saturates unexpectedly.
body: Magnetic field strength (H) is the field the current source produces. Magnetic flux density (B) is the field that includes the material's response. Confusing units for the two lands you in the wrong part of a B–H curve.

> 1 A/m = 0.01257 Oe (Oe = oersted)
> 1 Oe = 79.577 A/m ≈ 79.58 A/m
> Amp-turn (At) is current × turns; 1 At on 1 m mean path = 1 A/m
A/m: SI-strict transformer and coil design, magnetic hysteresis loop axes. Oersted: US permanent-magnet datasheets, magnetic-particle NDT, legacy motor design. Amp-turn: solenoid and relay design.

A solenoid with 1000 turns and 0.5 A over a 0.1 m core produces H = NI/ℓ = 500 / 0.1 = 5000 A/m = 62.8 Oe. On a soft-iron B–H curve this is well below saturation (~15000 A/m). Read the datasheet as gauss/oersted, work in A/m internally, cross-check.
H drives B through μ. A/m in SI, Oe in datasheets, amp-turn in windings.

faqs.a: In US and some legacy datasheets, yes. Modern SI-consistent datasheets use A/m.

faqs.q: How does H relate to coercivity?
faqs.a: Coercivity is the H field needed to demagnetise a saturated material, reported in Oe or A/m — usually thousands of oersteds for rare-earth magnets.
